title: Three-phase power
formula: S = √3 VLL I; P = S PF; Q = S √(1 − PF²)
assumptions: Balanced sinusoidal three-phase model. Q relation assumes sinusoidal current; with harmonics, non-active power is not necessarily fundamental kVAR. Load example supplies educational input values, not an equipment specification; validate all job geometry and operating parameters before use.

title: Single-phase power
formula: S = V I; P = S PF; Q = S √(1 − PF²)
assumptions: Sinusoidal single-phase model. PF must be 0–1; harmonics require a more complete power analysis. Load example supplies educational input values, not an equipment specification; validate all job geometry and operating parameters before use.

title: Motor current estimate
assumptions: Balanced three-phase sinusoidal input model. Output power is shaft power; efficiency is a percentage, not an assumed default. This does not size protection or a VVVF input circuit. Load example supplies educational input values, not an equipment specification; validate all job geometry and operating parameters before use.

title: Motor efficiency
assumptions: Input and output measurements must describe the same operating point. Efficiency must not exceed 100%. Load example supplies educational input values, not an equipment specification; validate all job geometry and operating parameters before use.

title: Power factor
assumptions: Positive consuming load. P and S must describe the same measurement interval; true PF can differ from displacement cos φ. Load example supplies educational input values, not an equipment specification; validate all job geometry and operating parameters before use.

title: Motor shaft torque
assumptions: Steady shaft power at the entered speed; starting, braking and transient torque are not calculated. Load example supplies educational input values, not an equipment specification; validate all job geometry and operating parameters before use.

title: Synchronous speed and slip
formula: ns = 120 f / poles; slip = 100 (ns − n) / ns
assumptions: Enter the pole count explicitly. This motoring-mode tool accepts 0 ≤ n ≤ ns; generating operation is outside scope. Load example supplies educational input values, not an equipment specification; validate all job geometry and operating parameters before use.

title: Frequency and rotor speed
formula: ns = 120 f / poles; n = ns (1 − slip/100)
assumptions: Slip is explicitly entered. Frequency alone does not determine an induction motor’s loaded shaft speed. Load example supplies educational input values, not an equipment specification; validate all job geometry and operating parameters before use.

title: Theoretical passenger capacity
assumptions: Ideal kinematic estimate, not a rated/certified capacity or measured flow. Step width does not uniquely determine occupancy; enter occupancy explicitly. Load example supplies educational input values, not an equipment specification; validate all job geometry and operating parameters before use.

title: Gear reduction
formula: ratio = nin / nout; nout = nin / ratio
assumptions: One idealised reduction stage. Slip, losses and compound stages require separate treatment. Load example supplies educational input values, not an equipment specification; validate all job geometry and operating parameters before use.

title: Step speed from validated geometry
formula: v = (motor rpm / ratio) × teeth × chain pitch / 60
assumptions: Pitch-line chain-speed model using validated geometry. Enter the total reduction and actual chain pitch/tooth count. This is not an approved escalator speed selection. Load example supplies educational input values, not an equipment specification; validate all job geometry and operating parameters before use.

title: Electrical energy consumption
assumptions: Constant active power over the entered duration. For variable duty, integrate measured power or calculate separate periods; do not use shaft power as electrical input. Load example supplies educational input values, not an equipment specification; validate all job geometry and operating parameters before use.

title: Inclined rise / projection
formula: H = L sin θ; horizontal projection = L cos θ
assumptions: Inclined straight section only. Horizontal landings and transition curves are excluded. Does not specify clearances, support reactions or civil pit dimensions. Load example supplies educational input values, not an equipment specification; validate all job geometry and operating parameters before use.

title: Electrical and mechanical unit converter

fields.label: Value in the selected source unit

assumptions: Exact scale conversion for the selected pair. Plain values and engineering suffixes are accepted; pasted explicit units are checked against the selected source unit. Load example supplies educational input values, not an equipment specification; validate all job geometry and operating parameters before use.

title: Gear ratio from measured shaft speeds
assumptions: Positive steady shaft speeds with identified input/output shafts. This is a speed ratio, not proof of an approved gear arrangement. Load example supplies educational input values, not an equipment specification; validate all job geometry and operating parameters before use.
